title: parallel tool-call padding and graceful replay for idempotent result injection
author: Priya Shah
description: Motivation: Multi-tool call patterns can interleave streaming tokens from several tool responses and model completions. In practice we've seen two pain points: (1) small/fast tools producing very short streams cause jittered client rendering and premature finalization, and (2) transient infra failures cause tool results to be replayed in ways that break deterministic injection ordering or duplicate side-effects in downstream consumers. This PR implements a lightweight, backwards-compatible approach to (A) padded streaming for short tool responses to stabilize client UX, and (B) a graceful replay mechanism that preserves idempotent result injection ordering by using stable idempotency keys and a small, broker-local replay buffer. Summary of changes: 1) API surface: added optional query params + headers for callers to opt into padded-tool-streaming (padding_ms, min_tokens) and replay-mode (replay_strategy=idempotent|best-effort). These map to existing OpenAI-compat function_call options so SDKs can expose the same ergonomics. 2) Runtime: introduced a tool-stream wrapper that delays final newline/terminal token emission until padding window elapses for small responses and emits a synthetic 'streaming.pad' metadata event to indicate suppressed termination. Padding is bounded and opt-in per-call to avoid global latency impact. 3) Replays: added an idempotency token binding for tool calls (x-redwood-tool-idempotency) that persists the latest injected result metadata in a broker-local replay index for a short TTL (configurable, default 30s). On transient tool error + retry, the runtime will consult the index to replay the previous result instead of re-invoking the tool when strategy=idempotent. 4) Tool-result injection: augmented the result envelope with stable sequence markers (sequence_id, partial_index) and a signature HMAC header so clients and SDKs can detect duplicate injections reliably. 5) Compatibility: OpenAI-compat adapter now translates function_call:{name,args} into the equivalent padded/replay-enabled calls when callers set function_call_mode=compat_padded. 6) SDK/Docs: small changes in python/typescript SDKs to expose the new opt-in flags and examples in redwood-examples/chat-tooling showing cross-service replay-safe integrations. 7) Tests: added unit tests across runtime, adapter, and SDK layers plus an e2e flakey-test harness that deterministically simulates transient tool failures. Checklist: - [x] API shape design and wire-compat review - [x] Runtime wrapper implementation with bounded padding - [x] Idempotency and replay index (TTL + eviction) - [x] OpenAI-compat mapping for function_call_mode - [x] SDK flag exposures and examples - [x] Unit + integration + e2e tests - [x] Metrics + tracing for padding/replay events Rollout plan: feature is behind two opt-in flags: per-call headers/params and a runtime feature gate controlled by configuration (default off for hosted customers). We'll enable for internal dogfood first (redwood-internal) for 48h, then staged rollout to 10% of hosted traffic for 72h. Monitoring: new metrics added (tool_stream_padding_count, tool_replay_hit, tool_replay_miss, tool_replay_eviction) and tracing spans for padding/replay lifecycle. Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged. Padding and replay are opt-in and do not alter non-streaming or long-running tool flows. Migration notes for integrators: SDKs expose function_call_mode and padding options; recommend starting with replay_strategy=best-effort for non-idempotent integrations and switch to idempotent only for tools that are safe to replay or when clients provide compensating idempotency. Security: HMAC uses existing tenant key material; TTLs are short and entries are stored in broker-local memory only. Performance: microbenchmarks show median p95 end-to-end latency increase of <2ms when padding is enabled for small responses, with negligible impact on throughput due to the opt-in nature. Related: ENG-5221 covers replay safety design, ENG-5330 tracks SDK ergonomics.

review_comments: Miguel Alvarez: Asked for clarification on the HMAC key rotation implications and suggested using tenant KMS wrapper rather than raw keys. Author replied: switched to existing tenant-key HMAC util and added a note to security section.

Dana Li: Requested explicit backpressure behavior when padding is enabled under heavy load. Author replied: made padding bounded and opt-in, added metrics and a circuit-breaker that disables padding above configurable pending-streams threshold.

Ethan Browne: Noted a potential race where a replay hit could return stale content if tool side-effects continue to change; asked for stronger doc guidance. Author replied: added best-practice guidance and default replay TTL of 30s; recommended idempotent=true on tool contract for safe replay.
CI Bot: initial e2e failed due to a flaky test (test_tool_replay_index_eviction). Reran harness and all checks passed on second run.
release_notes: Adds opt-in padded streaming for short tool responses and an idempotent replay mode to enable safe retries and deterministic result injection. Exposed via per-call flags and SDK ergonomics. Backwards compatible and disabled by default.
